hook: A short, gentle file about a character called Fred who lives inside books and hops from one story to the next. Go in expecting whimsy rather than horror. The fun is in how dryly the Foundation manages a resident whose only demand is something new to read.
whyItMatters: It shows that a Safe object with no real threat can carry a whole file on charm alone. Its premise, a being made entirely of text, turns the documents the Foundation produces into a possible living space. Fred reads less like a monster than an odd tenant, and the file treats him with matching patience.
thingsToNotice:
The containment rules quietly set up the joke: every scrap of paper leaving the room is searched for Fred and then burned anyway, and his nightly stay in a numbered journal reads like a bedtime arrangement, with lost reading material as the penalty. His discovery is played just as softly, as an extra character in a secondhand Tom Sawyer who only gave himself away after sitting next to Moby Dick.

He can rewrite words but never pictures, so illustrations end up contradicting the story around them, a lovely small detail. The best payoff is the reminder to check handwritten notes for addenda from "Guest Researcher Fred," which hints that he may already be in the file you are reading. The last addendum, naming SCP-583 as a possible way to destroy him if circumstances change, casts a faint shadow over an otherwise cozy piece.

related.note: Named in an addendum as a possible way to get rid of Fred.
